short: The Soviet Union's first nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, plagued by severe accidents.
full:
Commissioned on 30 April 1961, K-19 was the lead ship of the Project 658 (Hotel-class) submarines and the first Soviet nuclear-powered vessel equipped with nuclear ballistic missiles. Rushed into service to match American naval advancements, its construction and operational history were marked by numerous devastating accidents, earning it the grim nickname "Hiroshima" among Soviet sailors. On its maiden voyage in July 1961, it suffered a catastrophic loss of coolant to its reactor, requiring the crew to jury-rig a cooling system while exposed to lethal doses of radiation.

Despite the extreme human cost, K-19 remained in service for decades, illustrating the intense pressures and safety compromises of the early Cold War arms race. The heroic actions of its crew in preventing a full reactor meltdown and a potential nuclear detonation were kept secret by the Soviet government for nearly thirty years. The submarine was eventually decommissioned on 19 April 1990 and scrapped in the early 2000s.
